children: State Bank of India Sponsored GDR RegS (NSE:SBIN) raised its External Benchmark Linked Rate to 8.15% after the RBI hike, warning higher rates may curb discretionary loan demand and slow credit growth, while advancing YONO Bharat for feature‑phone and Jan Dhan users and pushing for a UPI MDR to fund digital infrastructure as AI pilots are weighed against cost‑productivity gains.
: SBIN GDRs: SBI raised its External Benchmark Linked Rate to 8.15% (+25 bps) effective Oct 15, 2026, after RBI’s 25 bp repo hike; home loan-linked rates will reset accordingly.
: SBIN developing YONO Bharat for launch in 6–12 months to reach feature‑phone and Jan Dhan users. Aims to expand YONO users to ~300 million by 2030; digital transaction cost ~Re 1.
SBIN: Higher Rates Likely Clamp Demand
: SBIN: higher rates likely cut demand for discretionary loans more than productive lending; credit growth expected to moderate, with impact on volumes depending on borrowers' loan purpose.
SBIN Board Back MDR On UPI
: SBIN: Board member Setty backed introducing an MDR on UPI transactions to fund bank infrastructure and risk systems, and said banks will try to stop merchants passing charges to customers.
SBIN Exec: AI With Human Oversight
: SBIN exec Setty said SBI will judge digital and AI rollouts by cost vs. productivity gains; AI won’t fully replace staff and will need human oversight.
